chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khas'ami, who said:
We were with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in a group, when a man from the mawla of Abu Ja'far entered upon him, greeted him, then sat down and wept.
Then he said to him, 'May I be your ransom, I had given God a vow that if God healed me from something I feared for myself, I would give in charity all that I possess.'
And indeed God, the Mighty and Majestic, healed me from it, and I have moved my dependents from my house to a tent in the ruins of the Ansar, and I have carried all that I possess.
So I am selling my house and all that I possess and will give it in charity.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Go and appraise your house and all your belongings and what you possess at a fair price, and know that value.'
Then take a blank sheet and write upon it the total of what you appraised.
Then go to the most trustworthy of people in your own eyes and deliver the sheet to him and make a bequest to him.
And instruct him that if the event of death befalls you, he should sell your house and all that you possess and give it in charity on your behalf.
Then return to your house and manage your wealth as you were doing.
So you and your dependents eat as you used to eat.
Then look at everything you gave in charity, whether it was easy for you from charity or maintaining kinship or in channels of righteousness.
Write all of that and count it.
And when the beginning of the year comes, go to the man to whom you made the bequest and instruct him to bring out the sheet.
Then write the total of what you gave in charity and what you spent on maintaining kinship or righteousness in that year.
Then do the same in every year until you fulfill God with all that you vowed for Him.
And your house and your wealth will remain for you, if God wills.'
The man said, 'You have relieved me, O son of the Messenger of God, may God make me your ransom.'

key_terms.نَذْر: Vow or pledge made to God

ai.seo_question: How to fulfill a vow of giving all possessions in charity without losing one's home and wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of fulfilling vows proportionally rather than through immediate liquidation of all assets, preserving the vow-maker's livelihood. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a practical mechanism of appraisal and annual disbursement, ensuring the vow is fulfilled over time while maintaining social and economic stability for the family. This approach highlights the balance between religious devotion and practical financial management in Shia legal tradition.
